prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production 2D Assassin survivor animation for Grave Accord. Image 1 is the approved complete idle strip for this exact facing; it locks identity, camera and equipment grip. Image 2 is the original shipped single-facing seed. Both references show the required direction; do not invent an opposite-facing view. Preserve the same slim young adult man with tousled black hair, visible eyes, lower face covered by a high rust-red scarf, a single long torn rust-red cape, charcoal split tunic/trousers, layered dark bronze shoulder/forearm/knee armor, brown utility belt pouches, gloves and boots. ONE slender long brass-and-black carbine stays attached to the physical RIGHT hand at the rear trigger grip and LEFT hand under the fore-end. Keep both hands and the rigid weapon connected. Preserve cape/strap asymmetry and original layered shoulder shapes. No exposed mouth, hood, extra pistol, knife, second rifle or weapon swap. Use restrained dry black ink and matte opaque gouache, broad quiet color planes and selective practical contours. Avoid glossy gradients, excessive tiny scratches, decorative filigree or noise. Maintain two arms, two legs and one intact body/weapon in every pose.
Every pose faces SOUTH, toward the viewer in the exact original front/three-quarter game angle. Chest, head and boots stay toward the viewer; do not turn into an east/west side profile. Right rear-trigger hand stays on viewer LEFT; left forward-support hand on viewer RIGHT. Retain the original diagonal ready-gun angle.
Draw EXACTLY 6 full-body poses as one coherent dash sheet, arranged in a clear 3-column by 2-row grid, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. No additional figure. Action: One short grounded directional dodge: 1 full upright ready stance, 2 compress knees, 3 fast low weight-shift step, 4 compact transfer step, 5 plant/absorb the landing, 6 recover upright ready. Keep the same facing and camera in every pose. Keep BOTH hands securely on the SAME weapon with no new grip and only controlled cloth movement. No roll, somersault, huge leap, wing-like cape, clone, speed line, smoke or afterimage. Step STRAIGHT TOWARD THE VIEWER, screen DOWN, with a foreshortened front-facing stride. Keep the chest/head frontal throughout; never turn to an east or west profile.
Every pose is one complete independent drawn body at ONE common character scale calibrated from upright pose 1. Crouched and resting poses retain their naturally lower height. Use roomy clear gutters between all cells and generous padding around the ENTIRE body/weapon/cape, with a consistent ground baseline in each row. Genuine RGBA transparency: alpha zero outside each figure and between limbs/props. No floor, shadow, backdrop, haze, vignette, glow, particles, checker pattern, text, labels, frame numbers or grid lines. Keep a coherent animation rather than unrelated character illustrations.
